```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

OpenSearch stores documents in indexes, where you can search them and
calculate summaries such as counts or totals. A Shiny app can show search
results using each visitor's existing OpenSearch permissions.

`oauth_db_opensearch_api()` sends the visitor's access token with HTTPS
requests. You can use OpenSearch's JSON search language, aggregations, or
its SQL plugin. Search results keep their document structure, so you can
choose which fields to display. No database driver is needed.

## Try OpenSearch locally

Start Docker and run:

```{r demo}
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_demo("opensearch")
```

The demo starts OpenSearch with its Security plugin, Keycloak and a Shiny
app. Alice and Bob see their own documents, and **Try a write** checks that
their roles cannot change the index. Allow at least 2 GB of Docker memory.
See [Getting started](getting-started.html#build-a-small-app) for accounts
and cleanup, or `?oauth_db_demo` for editing the configuration.

## Settings for the example

Ask your administrator for an HTTPS cluster with the Security plugin and
OAuth bearer-token authentication enabled. A cluster that requires AWS
SigV4 authentication needs a different client.

| Setting | Where to get it |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | The cluster's API endpoint, rather than its Dashboards page |
| Index, such as `orders` | OpenSearch Dashboards' index list or your administrator |
| Issuer, client ID, secret | Your [app registration](getting-started.html#register-your-app) with the cluster's trusted provider |
| `search.read` | The example API scope; define it in your provider or replace it |

Register `http://localhost:8100` as the app's redirect URI. The provider
must issue tokens with the audience and role claims the cluster expects.
Save the registration in `.Renviron` and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_OPENSEARCH_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
```

## A complete app

Replace the cluster URL and index name. This example assumes the provider
exposes a `search.read` scope; use your own registration's scopes.

After signing in,
click **Load rows**. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

```{r app}
pkgs <- c("shiny", "shinyOAuth", "shinyOAuthDB", "mirai", "jsonlite")
for (pkg in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_OPENSEARCH_ISSUER")
)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "search.read")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    verbatimTextOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

fetch_rows <- function(database) {
  result <- database$database(
    "orders",
    body = list(size = 20L, query = list(term = list(country = "NL")))
  )
  result$hits
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())
  search <- oauth_db_opensearch_api(
    auth$connection,
    url = "https://search.example.org",
    required_scopes = "search.read"
  )
  query_task <- oauth_db_task(search, method = fetch_rows)
  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke()
  })
  output$rows <- renderPrint(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)
    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.
```

Run `source("example.R")`. The app waits for sign-in before making
requests and clears the output on sign-out. If your provider requires a
resource parameter or named token target, configure it in shinyOAuth and
pass the target name to the helper's `target` argument.

## Search results and aggregations

A search returns documents in `result$hits$hits`, totals in
`result$hits$total`, and summaries in `result$aggregations`. Nested values
stay as lists and large JSON integers remain strings. Select the fields
you need when building a table.

For example, aggregate an `orders` index by country:

```{r aggregation}
result <- search$search(
  "orders",
  body = list(
    size = 0L,
    aggs = list(countries = list(terms = list(field = "country")))
  )
)
result$aggregations$countries$buckets
```

An index can be a name, a pattern or a vector such as `c("orders-*", "archive")`.
Each search returns one page. Use `from`/`size` or a stable sort with
`search_after` to fetch more. See `?oauth_db_opensearch_api` for native
JSON requests and pagination options.

## SQL and native JSON requests

With the SQL plugin enabled, you can query an index using SQL. The user
needs permission for SQL, index reads and the required index metadata:

```{r sql}
page <- search$sql(
  "SELECT owner, total FROM orders WHERE country = ?",
  parameters = list(list(type = "keyword", value = "NL"))
)
page$schema
page$datarows
```

The result keeps the plugin's `schema`, `datarows` and any cursor.
Parameters use `?` placeholders with the plugin's typed descriptors, as
above. Use `$request()` for other JSON APIs or cursor pagination; close
unfinished cursors before switching accounts. See `?oauth_db_opensearch_api`
for request methods.

## Configure cluster authentication and permissions

Configure the Security plugin's
[OpenID Connect authentication](https://docs.opensearch.org/latest/security/authentication-backends/openid-connect/)
or [JWT authentication](https://docs.opensearch.org/latest/security/authentication-backends/jwt/).
The cluster must verify the token's issuer and audience, then map its user
and role claims to OpenSearch roles.

For JWT authentication, an HTTP authentication configuration includes:

```yaml
jwt_auth_domain:
  http_enabled: true
  transport_enabled: false
  order: 0
  http_authenticator:
    type: jwt
    challenge: false
    config:
      jwt_header: Authorization
      jwt_url_parameter: null
      subject_key: sub
      roles_key: roles
      required_issuer: https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
      required_audience: opensearch-reporting
      signing_key: |
        -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
        Replace with the trusted issuer's public signing key.
        -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
  authentication_backend:
    type: noop
```

Replace the placeholder key and apply the fragment using the Security
plugin's administration procedure. This static-key setup is also used by
the local demo. For discovery and rotating signing keys, use the OIDC
authenticator.

Grant roles access to the indexes and operations they need. Document-level
and field-level security can further restrict the records and fields a
visitor receives. A Dashboards login alone doesn't configure this API
access.

## Tokens, errors and TLS

Requests use the visitor's current token and discard results after
sign-out or account changes. POST searches and SQL don't retry
automatically. A timeout or sign-out stops the app waiting for results;
work already submitted can continue on the server.

Pass `ca_bundle` for a private certificate authority. If a Windows curl
build can't use your PEM bundle, set `CURL_SSL_BACKEND=openssl` in
`.Renviron` and restart R before loading the package. See
`?oauth_db_opensearch_api` for raw responses and error handling.
